title: Breaking and Building with Materials
seo_title: Year 2 Science: Breaking and Building with Materials Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Recognise that materials can be changed physically without changing their material composition and explore the effect of different actions on materials including bending, twisting, stretching and breaking into smaller pieces (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 2 science worksheets on breaking and building with materials: cutting, tearing and crushing, building and rebuilding with pieces, and choosing materials for a job. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Cutting makes smaller pieces of the same material. Pieces can build new things.
body_html:
How to think about it

We can break materials into pieces.

  • Cut, tear, crush or snap.
  • The pieces are still the same material.
  • Pieces can build something new.
Example

Crushed biscuit: still biscuit?

only the size changed

Answer: yes

Common mistakes

  • Thinking small pieces are a different material.
  • Choosing a material for its colour instead of what it can do.

faq.a: Yes. Cutting makes smaller pieces, but they are still the same material.

faq.q: How do we choose a material for a job?
faq.a: Think about what it must do: be strong, waterproof, see-through, bendy or soft, then pick a material with that property.
Build with blocks and rebuild into new shapes, cut paper into puzzles, and test which materials are best for a boat or a bag.
